name: python-exactness-unresolved
body:
The Python frontend must preserve the never-guess rule exactly as global.constraint.never-fabricate-edges and global.constraint.exactness-no-heuristic require: an edge is emitted only where `ty` resolves to a project symbol. Anything `ty` cannot resolve to a project symbol becomes an UnresolvedTarget with a category, never a fabricated FQN or edge.

Category mapping — evaluated in this precedence order, first match wins, so the categories never overlap:

1. Resolved to a project symbol (first-party code: a symbol in the discovered, emitted tree that is not stdlib and not dependency code) — emit the real calls/uses edge; no UnresolvedTarget.
2. `stdlib` — the target is described by ty's tool-bundled vendored typeshed stubs (the reference origin `Vendored`: the typeshed stubs shipped inside the frontend that describe the Python standard library). A stdlib target is NEVER mapped to `external` or `unknown`.
3. `external` — the target is dependency code that is neither a project symbol nor stdlib: a project `vendor/`/`third_party/` tree, or a module resolved from the host/installed environment (the reference origins `System`/`SystemVirtual`: `site-packages`, a virtualenv, an installed distribution, any other dependency environment the `ty` project context exposes).
4. `unknown` — the target lies inside the discovered scan root but is neither a project symbol, stdlib, nor dependency code (a dynamic/computed reference, or a name `ty` cannot bind). This is the residue category, never a catch-all over rules 2–3.

`Vendored` is not overloaded. It names ONLY ty's tool-bundled typeshed stubs (rule 2, `stdlib`). A project `vendor/` or `third_party/` directory is dependency code, NEVER stdlib (rule 3, `external`): although it sits under the project directory it is excluded from discovery (`vendor/`, domain.entity.scan-exclusion) or classified `external` by the `py` code-type arm (`third_party|thirdparty`, requirements.requirement.python-code-type), so it is never a project symbol and never stdlib. This matches how every other frontend classifies dependency trees — verified in src/classify.rs: Go `vendor`, Java `vendor|third_party|thirdparty`, C++ `vendor|third_party|thirdparty|external`, Rust `vendor`, TS `vendor`, C# `vendor|packages|bin|third_party|thirdparty` all map to `external`.

Precedence is load-bearing exactly where a single undifferentiated sentence collides: `stdlib` (rule 2) outranks `external` (rule 3), so a stdlib/typeshed target is `stdlib` even though it also lies outside the scan root; `external` (rule 3) outranks `unknown` (rule 4), so a vendored dependency copy is `external` even though it is not physically outside the project tree; `unknown` is only for in-root references that are neither.

Resolution is exact where `ty` resolves; there is no heuristic resolution pass and no reduced-resolution mode — under incremental emission the Python graph must equal the full-scan graph (exact-ongoing-equivalence).

AC: an unresolved third-party import, or a reference into a project `vendor/`/`third_party/` tree, yields an unresolved_call or unresolved_use to an UnresolvedTarget with category `external` (never `stdlib`); a reference into the Python standard library / ty's vendored typeshed yields category `stdlib` (never `external`); an in-root dynamic/unresolvable reference that is neither stdlib nor dependency yields category `unknown`; no guessed calls/uses edge is emitted.
